fields.meta_title: Contest Entry Form Builder With Entry Rules | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a contest entry form that checks eligibility and tags repeat entries, then draws winners from the entries that count. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Contest Entry Form That Counts Only Valid Entries
fields.hero_description: Build a contest entry form that turns away entrants who do not qualify and keeps every entry in a database you own.
fields.features_heading: What a Template Leaves You to Check by Hand
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the contest entry form and the entries table behind it, with the checks an organizer would otherwise run by hand.
fields.feature_1:
Eligibility checked before an entry saves

Ask for a birth date and a state, and the form turns away anyone under the minimum age or outside the states your rules allow. An entrant who does not qualify never reaches the draw.
fields.feature_2:
Repeat entries tagged, never deleted

Each new entry is matched on email and phone against everyone who has already entered. A second entry from the same address is saved with a duplicate tag and left out of the count.
fields.feature_3:
Word limits and file types held on submit

Take the entry itself as pasted text or as an upload. Set a word limit or the file types you accept, and the form refuses an entry that breaks either rule and tells the entrant why.
fields.feature_4:
A random draw that names alternates

Draw a winner and as many alternates as your rules name, picked at random from valid entries only. Each draw is saved with its time and the number of entries it was drawn from.
fields.feature_5:
Score sheets for a judging panel

Give each judge a private view of the entries, with entrant names hidden if you ask. Judges score against the criteria in your rules, and the app averages scores into a ranked list.
fields.feature_6:
Next season's contest starts from this code

Export the full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can change the rules, add a new prize or a new entry type, and run the same contest again next year.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Contests That Run on Entry Rules
fields.tab_content_1:
Of the 1,316 entries, 32 repeats sit out the draw

Halfmoon Coffee Roasters is giving away a year of coffee to US residents aged 18 and over, one entry per email. Of 1,316 entries, 32 reuse an address that already entered and carry a duplicate tag. The draw picks Ruth Ambrose as winner, plus two alternates, from the 1,284 entries that remain.
fields.tab_content_2:
Any story over 2,500 words goes back to its writer

Alder Bend Public Library runs a short story contest for teen writers. The form counts the words in each pasted story before saving it. Entry 0147 arrived at 2,740 words and went back with a note to cut 240. Each writer's birth date files the story in the 13 to 15 or 16 to 18 bracket for judging.
fields.tab_content_3:
Each friend who enters adds one entry, up to five

Every listener who enters the Pocket Atlas gear giveaway gets a personal share link. A friend who enters through that link earns the sharer one bonus entry, and bonus entries stop at five. Lena Okonjo brought in 7 friends and holds 6 entries in the draw: her own and 5 bonus.
fields.tab_content_4:
One vote per confirmed email, and Riverlight wins with 412

Three designs reached the final round of the Merrow Falls mural contest. Each resident votes once, and a vote counts only after the voter clicks the link sent to their email. Voting closed with 1,006 confirmed votes: Riverlight 412, Tin Roof 389, and Cornfield 205.

fields.howto_title: How to Build a Contest Entry Form
fields.howto_description: These seven steps take a contest entry form from official rules to a winner drawn from valid entries.
fields.howto_step_1_des: Set out who can enter, the entry period, the prize, and how the winner is chosen before any field exists. For a random draw, explain how the draw works. For a judged contest, list the criteria judges will score. Every check the form runs comes from this page.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Pick a minimum age and the states or countries your rules allow. Add a birth date field and a location field so the form can test both before an entry saves. If staff and their households cannot enter, add a question that asks.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Choose one entry per person, or one plus a bonus entry for each referral up to a cap. Decide whether email or phone number identifies a person. Then write the limit into the rules in the same words the form uses.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Paste the rules into one prompt and say whether each entry carries a photo, a story, or contact details alone. Emergent builds the form and a table that stores every entry. Ask for a change in plain words, and the form updates to match.
fields.howto_step_5_title: 05 Choose a draw or a judging panel
fields.howto_step_5_des: A random draw should name alternates in case a winner never replies. A judged contest needs a scoring view for each judge that rates every entry on the criteria you wrote. Pick one method per contest and name it in the rules.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Plan the close and the winner email
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pick the exact closing minute and name its time zone in the rules. Write the email the winner receives, with a deadline to reply. Alternates get a message of their own, sent only if the winner lets that deadline pass without an answer.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Enter twice from one email and confirm the second entry carries a duplicate tag. Then enter as someone under the age limit and check that the form turns you away. Run a test draw on a copy of the entries table before the real one.

faq_plan.q: What is a contest entry form?
faq_plan.a: A contest entry form is the form people fill in to enter a contest, giveaway, or sweepstakes. It records who entered, how to reach them, and that they accepted the official rules. For a judged contest, it also carries the entry itself, such as a photo or a short story.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a contest entry form?
faq_plan.a: Write the official rules first, then describe the contest and who can enter in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. It builds the form and the database of entries behind it. Publish the rules at a link of their own and put that link on the form before you share it.

faq_plan.q: What fields should a giveaway entry form include?
faq_plan.a: Keep it short: name, email, a birth date or age confirmation, state or country, and a required checkbox that links to the official rules. Add a phone number only if you plan to call winners. Ask for a shipping address from the winner after the draw, not from every entrant.

faq_plan.q: What should I change in a contest entry form template before launch?
faq_plan.a: Change the fields to match your official rules: the minimum age, the states allowed, the entry limit, and the closing time. Then add the rules checkbox and a confirmation message that says when the winner is drawn. Pair the form with a giveaway landing page that shows the prize and the deadline next to a link to the rules.

faq_plan.q: Does a sweepstakes entry form need different fields than a contest one?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when judges pick the contest winner. If the winner comes from a random draw, the form needs contact and eligibility fields only. If judges pick the winner, add a field for the entry itself and show the judging criteria beside it. Before you add any purchase or payment step, check the rules that apply to your promotion.

faq_plan.q: How do I handle duplicate entries on a contest entry form?
faq_plan.a: Have the form compare each new entry's email address with the entries already saved. Keep a repeat as a tagged row instead of removing it, which lets you answer an entrant who asks why only one entry counted. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps. A giveaway that draws thousands of entries keeps every row.

faq_plan.q: How do I get feedback from people who filled in my contest entry form?
faq_plan.a: Send a short follow-up form to everyone who entered once the winner is announced. Ask how they heard about the contest, whether the rules were clear, and whether they would enter again, each on a 1 to 5 scale. Keep it as brief as a training feedback form: three or four questions at most.

faq_plan.q: How do I pick a random winner from contest entry form responses?
faq_plan.a: Draw only from entries that passed your checks. Pick the alternates in the same draw and in order, and the second name is ready if the winner never replies. Keep the draw record until the prize is delivered, in case an entrant asks how the winner was chosen.

faq_plan.q: Can contest entry forms accept photo and video uploads?
faq_plan.a: They can when you add an upload field. Make it a required field of its own, and accept only the file types your judges can open, such as JPG or MP4. Print the size limit next to the field where entrants see it before they upload. With Emergent, each upload lands in the same database row as the entrant's name and email, and you own that database.

faq_plan.q: How do I contact the winner from a contest entry form?
faq_plan.a: Email the winner at the address on their entry, with a deadline to reply and a request to confirm their age and state against the eligibility rules. Once they confirm, collect a shipping address for the prize. If the prize is cash and your finance team pays by check, send it through a check request form with the winner's details attached.

plan.angle: The top 10 is template galleries from form builders (SurveyMonkey, Gravity Forms, Jotform, Formstack, Formfacade), two blog explainers, a video and a card listing. Every result stops at collecting names and emails. This page shows the work an organizer does after entries arrive: turning away entrants who do not qualify, tagging repeat entries, holding a written entry to its word limit, counting referral bonus entries up to a cap and running a one-vote-per-email public vote, with every entry kept as a row the organizer owns. The FAQ answers the setup, giveaway, sweepstakes and template questions builders ask.
